These are the declarations in the REST module (`openmrs-module-webservices.rest`) that call `LocationService.saveLocation`, in order of likely impact. Everything is under `omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/`. I found them with one regex search for `saveLocation(` and read the surrounding lines of the two production files. I didn't check for indirect callers, such as other resources that delegate to these ones.

1. `LocationResource1_8.save(Location)` (line 222) returns `Context.getLocationService().saveLocation(location)`. This is the main `/location` resource save path. It handles create and update through `DelegatingCrudResource`, and the return value is used directly.
2. `LocationAttributeResource1_9`, the `/location/{uuid}/attribute` sub-resource, calls it in two places:
   - The method ending at line 103 adds the attribute to the location, then calls `saveLocation(delegate.getLocation())` at line 101. Attribute creation and update depend on the parent location being saved.
   - `delete(...)` (lines 110-114) voids the attribute and then calls `saveLocation` on the parent at line 113. A voided attribute is only persisted through this call.

The only other callers are in a test class, `omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs1_9/LocationController1_9Test.java` (lines 164, 225, 242). That test calls the service directly to set up data, so a behaviour change could break its setup.
